# Create Custom Genmoji and Images with Apple Intelligence

> **In short:** Apple Intelligence turns a text description like "cat astronaut on a skateboard" into a custom emoji (a Genmoji) or a small image you can drop into Messages, Notes, or any chat. You need a recent iPhone or iPad, the latest iOS update, and Apple Intelligence turned on.

By the end of this guide, you'll be able to type a quick idea, watch Apple Intelligence draw it, and send it as a sticker or custom emoji in your next conversation. This is for anyone with a supported iPhone or iPad, an Apple ID, and a few minutes to try.

## Before you start

- **Device**: iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max, any iPhone 16 or 17 model, or an iPad with an M1 chip or newer. Older devices can't run Apple Intelligence.
- **Software**: iOS 18.1 or later for Genmoji, iOS 18.2 or later for the standalone Image Playground app. Update in **Settings → General → Software Update**.
- **Apple ID**: signed in on the device, with the region and language set to a country Apple Intelligence supports (US English is the broadest option).
- **Apple Intelligence setting**: turned on. The feature is free with supported devices, no extra plan needed, though the first time you turn it on you may be placed on a short waitlist.
- **Time**: about 5 minutes the first time, then under a minute once you know the flow.

## Step 1 — Turn on Apple Intelligence

Open the **Settings** app (the gray gear icon on your home screen), scroll down, and tap **Apple Intelligence & Siri**. If you see a button that says **Turn On Apple Intelligence**, tap it. If instead you see **Join the Apple Intelligence Waitlist**, tap that — Apple adds new users in batches, so you may wait a few hours to a few days. While you wait, Genmoji and Image Playground won't appear yet, so it's a good moment to think of a few fun ideas to try later.

💬 Example: while you wait, jot down three ideas you'd love to see drawn, like "sleepy sloth with coffee" or "your pet in a cape."

You'll know it worked when Settings shows a line near the top that says something like "Apple Intelligence is Ready."

## Step 2 — Open Image Playground

You can start in two places. The first is the standalone **Image Playground** app — search your home screen, or swipe down on the home screen and type "Image Playground" to find it. The second is from inside Messages, Notes, or Freeform: tap the **+** or **Apps** icon next to the text field, then pick **Image Playground** from the list. Both paths open the same screen, with a blank preview area at the top and a text box at the bottom that prompts you to describe an image. The standalone app gives you more room to experiment, so it's the friendlier starting point.

If neither option appears, your device or iOS version probably doesn't support Apple Intelligence — go back to "Before you start" and double-check.

💬 Example: open the standalone app so you have full screen to play with.

You'll know it worked when you see an empty preview at the top and a text box at the bottom ready for your description.

## Step 3 — Type what you want to see

Tap the text box at the bottom of the screen and write a short, clear description of the picture you have in mind. A few specific details work better than a long paragraph — think of it as giving directions to a friend, not writing a novel. After a second or two, Apple Intelligence shows several preview images above the box, each in a slightly different style. To try new ideas, edit your words rather than starting over; the previews refresh in a couple of seconds. If the first results miss the mark, rephrase instead of regenerating — swapping one word often changes the whole image.

💬 Example: "a happy golden retriever wearing a tiny wizard hat, cartoon style."

You'll know it worked when you see at least one preview you actually like, even if it's not perfect yet.

## Step 4 — Choose a style and refine

Above the previews you'll see style options, usually **Animation**, **Illustration**, and **Sketch**. Tap each one to see the same idea in a different look — Animation feels smooth and slightly 3D, Illustration is a flat friendly drawing, and Sketch looks like a pencil drawing. Swipe through the previews to find a version you like, and tap a preview to open it full size. If the image is close but not quite right, change one or two words in your description (try swapping "happy" for "curious" or adding "with a red collar") and watch the previews update live.

One honest note: Image Playground leans toward illustrated, stylized results. It can draft a fun image in seconds, but it cannot make photorealistic photos or perfectly match every tiny detail you describe.

You'll know it worked when you find a preview you'd happily send to a friend.

## Step 5 — Save or share your image

When you have a preview you like, tap it to open the full version. From there, tap **Done** to keep it in your Image Playground library, or tap the **Share** button (a square with an arrow pointing up) to send it to Messages, Mail, Notes, or any other app that accepts images. You can also tap **More** to copy the image or save it to your Photos. Anything you create stays on your device by default, so you can experiment without worrying about your prompts being shared.

💬 Example: tap Share, choose Messages, pick a chat, hit Send, and your drawing arrives as a sticker-style image.

You'll know it worked when your image shows up in the conversation exactly the way it looked in the preview.

## Step 6 — Make a custom Genmoji in Messages

Genmoji (a custom emoji made by Apple Intelligence) lives right inside Messages. Open any conversation, tap the **emoji** button (the smiley face) in the text field, then look for a colorful **Genmoji** icon near the top — it often looks like a smiley face with a sparkle or glow. Tap it, then type a description in the search bar. Apple Intelligence creates several custom emoji based on your words. Tap the one you like, and it sends just like a regular emoji. If you don't see a Genmoji icon, your iOS may be earlier than 18.1, or Apple Intelligence may still be processing — check the Settings screen from Step 1.

💬 Example: type "sleepy sloth drinking coffee" — a perfect Monday morning chat reaction.

You'll know it worked when your custom emoji shows up in the message bubble, sized like any other emoji.

## Common mistakes

- **Writing a description that's too long.** "Friendly humanoid robot with three arms, wearing a beret, painting a purple and orange sunset" is too much. **Fix**: keep it under about 10 words. "Robot painting a sunset" gives much better results.
- **Expecting a photorealistic photo.** Image Playground is designed for illustrated, friendly images. **Fix**: if you want photo-style results, this isn't the right tool — try a different image generator instead.
- **Not seeing the Genmoji button in Messages.** Usually this means your iOS is older than 18.1, or Apple Intelligence is still finishing setup. **Fix**: open Settings → General → Software Update, install the latest iOS, then re-check the Apple Intelligence & Siri screen.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** send a one-of-a-kind "happy birthday" sticker to a friend, react to a group chat with a custom emoji no one else has, or make a quick visual for a family message — no design skills needed.
- **For your work or business:** sketch a concept for a slide or social post in seconds and drop it into a Message or email as a quick visual aid when you don't have time to open a design tool.
- **If you're just getting started:** try the Image Playground app first because the bigger canvas makes it easier to experiment, then move on to Genmoji in Messages once you feel comfortable.

## Try it now

Open Image Playground and type "pizza slice wearing sunglasses at the beach" — see what Apple Intelligence draws, then send it to your favorite chat and watch the reaction.
